parsed_output.analysis: The model correctly captures: the initial transition into HumanDriving on Power On (spec 3), HumanDriving as a simple state (spec 1), Autonomous as a compound state with sub-states (spec 2), and the front_distance > 10 guard for entering Autonomous (spec 4). Two non-conformances are identified: (1) the return-to-HumanDriving transition is mis-placed and mis-conditioned, and (2) the Power Off transition is missing from the Autonomous state.

issues.issue: The transition back to HumanDriving is placed on the parent Autonomous state with 'in (AutoFinal)' as an OR-condition alongside the events, rather than being a transition from the AutoFinal sub-state triggered by the events alone.
issues.reason: Spec item 5 says: 'transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final).' The phrase 'in (auto final)' identifies the source sub-state (AutoFinal), not an additional alternative trigger. The correct modelling is a transition from AutoFinal to HumanDriving with the guard 'human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed'. As written in the model, being in AutoFinal by itself would be sufficient to fire the transition (since it is OR-ed), which is not what the spec intends.

issues.issue: The Power Off transition to the final state is only defined from HumanDriving. There is no Power Off transition from the Autonomous state (or its sub-states).
issues.reason: Spec item 6 states: 'when power off, it will transit to final state.' This is a system-level requirement with no restriction on the current state. The model should also allow a Power Off transition from Autonomous (or from its sub-states) to the final state, so that the system can be powered off regardless of which mode it is in.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
